mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in the unemployment rate signals a strong economy with tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to rising interest rates and reduced corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer demand indicated by rising residential sales (RSAFS), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 trading days due to elevated corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases over 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, it signals an overheated labor market that may prompt aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening economy with housing sector recovery, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate central bank stimulus.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines and HOUST rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a stagflationary regime characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO) and rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative returns over the next 20 trading days due to deteriorating corporate profit margins and central bank hawkishness.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
